Would You Pay New Prius Money for This Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat?
21 photos
Photo: Instagram | phoenix_motor_collection
Everyone and their pet knows that the Dodge Challenger is no longer in production. The third generation was dropped in 2023, as that’s when the final copy rolled off the assembly line at the Brampton facility in Ontario, Canada.
However, just because one machine is no longer being put together does not make it less exciting. Most gearheads still dream about an older supercar, and some would gladly live with a proper muscle car that packs so much oomph that it can give blue-blooded exotics a run for their money. And this is definitely where the Hellcat lineup fits, because even in its most basic configuration, it offered more than enough power for exciting daily drives sprinkled with fast takeoffs.
The original Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat came out more than a decade ago as a high-performance variant of the brand’s muscle car. It had a more aggressive look on the outside, the cockpit was bedecked with some extras, and the chassis was modified. The brakes were also uprated in order to cope with the extra oomph. The model came with two separate key fobs. The black one limited the output to a more down-to-earth 500 horsepower (373 kW507 ps), whereas the red one enabled the full output capability.
This meant 707 horsepower (527 kW/717 ps), with the peak thrust being rated at 650 pound-feet (881 Nm). The 6.2-liter supercharged V8 engine, which was also introduced not only to the Challenger’s four-door sibling, the era’s Charger, but also to the Jeep Grand Cherokee Trackhawk (previous generation) and the Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat, enabled 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) in a little over 3.5 seconds. It had a 199 mph (320 kph) top speed, and could complete the 1/4-mile in 11.6 seconds at 125 mph (201 kph) on stock rubber.
Photo: Instagram | phoenix_motor_collection From here on, Dodge kept refining the Hellcat motor , launching punchier versions of its third-gen Challenger. Some of them exceeded the 800-horsepower mark, and the fastest and most powerful production muscle car to date remains the SRT Demon 170. This model ran the standing quarter mile in 8.91 seconds, with an exit speed of 151.17 mph (243.28 kph), had up to 1,025 horsepower in its top configuration, and reached 60 mph (97 kph) in a neck-snapping 1.66 seconds.
Pictured in the gallery is a 2016 model year Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat, which had 31,794 miles (51,167 km) under its belt at the time of cataloging. Thus, it’s far from being a barely-driven copy, as it has seen plenty of action over the years. However, it still looks very good, as the glossy black paint finish is on the shiny side of things. There are some red emblems on the outside, red brake calipers behind the black wheels, as well as a vented hood, and a ducktail spoiler that came from the factory.
This machine features a black leather interior and black trim. It also has white stitching for contrast, the usual SRT inserts, and there is plenty of wear on the driver’s seat. But then again, you didn’t think that it would be in top notch form, did you?
The vendor mentions stuff such as the leather upholstery, heated and ventilated front seats, heated steering wheel, and Harman Kardon audio system. The Bluetooth connectivity, Apple CarPlay, air conditioning, and navigation system are also on deck, and so are the rear parking sensors, reversing camera, and blind spot monitoring system.
Photo: Instagram | phoenix_motor_collection This Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat also has a few modifications, and the selling dealer says that it is in “mint condition.” The muscle car has reportedly never been involved in an accident, as per the clean Carfax history report mentioned in the listing. It has a clean title, and you can park it in your driveway if you really want it. By the way, the vendor also offers financing.
Speaking of the vendor, it is known as @phoenix_motor_collection on Instagram, and advertises this machine on its social media, which is where we found it. But how much does it cost to park this thing in your driveway? Well, at the time of writing, the muscle car in question had an asking price of $46,400 attached to it.
That’s basically new, range-topping Toyota Prius PHEV money, and most petrolheads and their grandmothers would tell you that you only live once, and it’s better to own a great V8-powered ride rather than a dull electrified compact. But let’s not forget that the latter comes with the factory warranty, and only the delivery miles under its belt, whereas the former has seen a lot of action over the years, and there is obviously no warranty here.
Still, if you crave a nice Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat and have less than $50,000 to blow on one, then this example could be exactly what the doctor ordered. And if you must have it, then you know what to do next, don’t you? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Phoenix Motor Collection (@phoenix_motor_collection)
